candidates.summary: isCrossingCurParam dropped the realm static-type test the three write rules carried, so any name `cur` declared in a crossing function's own block is unwritable whatever its type
candidates.failure_scenario: func sum(_ realm, n int) int { cur := 0; for i := 0; i < n; i++ { cur += i }; return cur } no longer compiles: the unnamed first realm parameter (.arg_0) leaves the function crossing while the FuncDecl block owns an int named cur, so isCrossingCurParam resolves the declaring node, returns true, and the assignment rule panics "cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter". Same for a named result (cur int) written, address-taken (&cur, message: "realm-typed `cur`") or range-assigned. 56 `(_ realm` signatures exist under examples/ at this sha, and `cur` is an ordinary cursor name. All four shapes run on the merge base b7845fb2d and are rejected at head, against the PR body's Compatibility claim that the write rules only got narrower.
candidates.verify_by: cp reviews/.../tests/b1-removed-nonrealm-cur-binding.gno into gnovm/tests/files/zrealm_cur_nonrealm_local.gno and run go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_cur_nonrealm' -v at 6d88deba7, then again after git checkout b7845fb2da9a21bfb895e1c008f016776f8342d0 -- gnovm/pkg/gnolang/preprocess.go
candidates.evidence: head 6d88deba7, four files: 'unexpected panic: .../zrealm_cur_nonrealm_local.gno:8:2-10: cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter', '.../zrealm_cur_nonrealm_assign.gno:8:2-9: cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter', '.../zrealm_cur_nonrealm_ref.gno:5:7-11: cannot take the address of a realm-typed `cur`', '.../zrealm_cur_nonrealm_range.gno:5:2-6:3: cannot assign to a realm-typed `cur` in a range clause'; with base preprocess.go only: '--- PASS: TestFiles/zrealm_cur_nonrealm_local.gno', '--- PASS: TestFiles/zrealm_cur_nonrealm_assign.gno', '--- PASS: TestFiles/zrealm_cur_nonrealm_ref.gno', '--- PASS: TestFiles/zrealm_cur_nonrealm_range.gno'. The same predicate also refuses the realm-typed named result the reviewer thread names (func f(_ realm) (cur realm) { cur = nil }): that one panics at head and at b7845fb2d alike, so it is a member of the class finding 2 claims to fix rather than a regression. The reviewer's proposed `ft.Params[0].Name == "cur"` conjunct closes both.

candidates.summary: TestFuncDisplayName pins only the branch a real func literal never takes, leaving the rewritten panic's literal path untested
candidates.failure_scenario: funcDisplayName's second branch (fv.Source != nil, "%s func literal at %s:%d") is what every runtime func literal takes, since doOpFuncLit sets Source (op_expressions.go:779). The test asserts the Name branch and the Source==nil fallback "<func literal>", which only a FuncValue with no source reaches. Change the location format, or lose GetLocation's File/Line, and the message the PR's finding 4 exists to produce degrades with every test still green.
candidates.verify_by: read gnovm/pkg/gnolang/op_call_test.go:110-118 against funcDisplayName at op_call.go:567; grep 'Source:' for the FuncValue built by doOpFuncLit (op_expressions.go:779). Then add a crossing func-literal backstop filetest and confirm the panic text is 'func literal at <file>:<line>'.
candidates.evidence: op_expressions.go:779 'Source:     x,' in the FuncValue built for a FuncLitExpr; values.go:717 treats fv.Source == nil as the unset case.

candidates.summary: the harness carve-out drops the identity check for every no-cross crossing entry dispatched by package testing, not only the cur the harness seeds
candidates.failure_scenario: harnessSeedsCur keys on the caller frame's PkgPath alone, so any crossing function a realm test enters without cross() from a testing-package frame skips realmMatchesCurHIV. A realm test that forwards a stale or sibling cur through a testing-dispatched call passes under gno test while the same call panics on chain, which is the failure the check was added to surface to the author.
candidates.verify_by: narrow the exemption to the seeded value: compare fr.Cur against the cur the top-level test frame holds, rather than exempting the whole caller package; then re-run go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestStdlibs/test-testing' and the new cur_subtest_test.gno
